title: Xinran Zhou
text: INTERDISCIPLINARY ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH Xinran Zhou Environmental economics · Ecosystem science · Geospatial analysis I use quantitative methods to examine environmental and economic questions in agriculture, ecosystems, and land management. Email LinkedIn ABOUT ME Background and research interests I am completing a Professional Science Master’s in Ecosystem Science & Sustainability (Carbon Management) at Colorado State University, while pursuing an M.S. in Population, Resources & Environmental Economics at Shandong University. I earned a B.A. in Economics from China University of Geosciences (Wuhan). My experience spans life cycle assessment and costing, ecosystem modeling workflows, geospatial analysis, and quantitative economics—including panel-data econometrics, evolutionary game modeling, and agricultural input–output data analysis. I am interested in the economic feasibility and environmental trade-offs of agricultural and land-management decisions across different landscapes. title: Research and Technical Experience
text: Research and Technical Experience Selected Research Environmental and economic assessment of synthetic humic substances This research at Shandong University evaluates four synthetic humic substance production pathways and their agricultural applications in China. A regionalized LCA-LCC framework compares environmental impacts, production costs, and monetized environmental externalities across crop systems, regions, and electricity scenarios. View slides (PDF) · Download PowerPoint Forest cover change across Colorado’s Front Range, 2001–2021 Collaborative research at CU Boulder’s Environmental Data Science Innovation and Impact Lab (ESIIL) examines forest-cover change across Colorado’s Front Range. Python and Google Earth Engine workflows combine land-cover, elevation, and burned-area data to analyze land-cover transitions and spatial patterns of forest loss. View slides (PDF) · Download PowerPoint Collaborative ESIIL research with Camille Guillen, Malia Goldstein, Mohammad Saif, and Sandra M. Duran. Wind power policy and corporate sustainability This study examines how wind-power policy instruments relate to corporate sustainability using panel data from 58 listed firms between 2009 and 2021. Two-way fixed-effects models are complemented by mechanism, robustness, and heterogeneity analyses across ownership types and regions. Renewable Portfolio Standards A tripartite evolutionary game model examines interactions among government, renewable-energy producers, and consumers under Renewable Portfolio Standards. MATLAB simulations and sensitivity analyses explore how certificate prices, penalties, and transaction costs affect stakeholder strategies. Model Testing and Data Work MEMS Grazing Scheduler testing Technical work at LandEngine, Colorado State University, involved testing the MEMS Grazing Scheduler, reviewing model outputs, and documenting the workflow. China-specific FABIO framework Work on a China-specific Food and Agriculture Biomass Input-Output (FABIO) framework harmonizes agricultural, biomass, economic, and environmental data. Product-level flow accounts, mappings for 84 agricultural products, and environmental satellite accounts connect agricultural flows with environmental pressures. Collaborative research with Xiaotian Ma, Jinglan Hong, Nan Li, Ming Xu, Tianjie Lei, and Honglin Zhong.
